name: Maoism–Third Worldism
summary: Maoism–Third Worldism combines Marxism-Leninism-Maoism with a dependency-theory view that the First World is a parasitic exploiter bloc whose workers form a labor aristocracy bought off with surplus extracted from the Third World. It holds that the real revolutionary proletariat lies in Asia, Africa and Latin America and that global people's war by oppressed nations is the path to communism, with the First World's role being mainly to be defeated or to repay its debt.

missingStatements.text: Workers in rich countries are mostly not exploited, and share in the profits that rich countries extract from poor ones.
missingStatements.rationale: Sunrise and RAIM both hold that the first-world masses have no significant exploited groups and are net beneficiaries of the third world's exploitation.

quotes.text: There is no Western proletariat. There are no significant exploited social groups in the first world.

Both Maoist-Third Worldists and RAIMers agree that the vast majority of First Worlders are among the exploiting classes; that First World workers receive enough of a benefit to make it to where that absorb more value than they create and thus are themselves net-exploiters.

name: Marxism-Leninism-Maoism-Third Worldism
aliases.quote: Maoism-Third Worldism is a shorter name for Marxism-Leninism-Maoism-Third Worldism.

keyFigures.role: Author of Settlers: The Mythology of the White Proletariat, the labor-aristocracy account that RAIM and Maoism-Third Worldists cite

evidence.quote: In Settlers , J. Sakai explores the history of First World White workers in betraying the interests of oppressed and colonized people in North America and elsewhere. Sakai was widely criticized as “writing off” White workers. How does How Maoism-Third Worldism see an issue like this?

Maoism-Third Worldism has set about looking at modern social configurations relative to the revolutionary struggle. In this regard, Maoist-Third Worldists follows Mao, who expounded on the importance of uniting real friends of the revolution against real enemies of the revolution. Actually, the first words of Selected Readings from the Works of Mao are, “Who are our enemies? Who are our friends?” I know that some First Worldist, nominal “Maoists” get teary-eyed at the thought of disregarding and denigrating their beloved First World or white “proletariat,” but RAIM and the LLCO movement don’t have time for sentimentality. We need to know how social classes actually line up, in order to inform a correct practice. If the First World had some amount of a proletariat capable of standing on its own, one would think the various First Worldists would have something to show for it. But they don’t. Instead of complaining about how Sakai, RAIM or the LLCO ‘writes off’ this or that group, First Worldists should account for their own inability to gain traction with virtually any segment of First World society outside of small academic and activist circles. Sakai, RAIM and LLCO all contribute to an analysis which explains why things happen like they do; we’re not to be blame for the facts, especially when we’re talking about a historical analysis.

In Settlers , J. Sakai explores the history of First World White workers in betraying the interests of oppressed and colonized people in North America and elsewhere. Sakai was widely criticized as “writing off” White workers. How does How Maoism-Third Worldism see an issue like this?

What should people be reading to learn more about Maoism-Third Worldism? Monkey Smashes Heaven is published by the Leading Light Communist Organization. It can be found at: http://llco.org/msh There is also a Polish Maoist-Third Worldist website at http://trzeciswiat.wordpress.com/ As far as other readings, I would suggest ‘Mao Zedong on the Chinese Revolution’ by Chen Boda for a really systemic overview on Maoism, as well as ‘Long Live the Victory of People’s War’ by Lin Biao. Otherwise, Monkey Smashes Heaven has a fairly large reading list at http://llco.org/archives/9102 It contains a lot of the Marxist classics. Settlers is on there, as well as a limited selection from MIM.

evidence.quote: There has not been an official title, but Maoism-Third Worldism is becoming the most excepted term for this stage. The difficulty arises out of the vague beginnings of the ideology. As Mao Zedong fell to revisionism, just as Stalin had, Lin Biao gave a few ideas as to how the next stage could be formulated. He, unfortunately, died before any real concrete theory could be put forward. The most important work, representing a kind of foundation is “Long Live the Victory of People’s War”.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: The Essentials text says people's relationship with non-human life must more closely resemble the relationship socialism seeks among people.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: In the Stolen at Gunpoint interview Sakai says the Southwest was stolen at gunpoint, was never legally part of the United States and was taken by plain conquest in 1848.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: Lin Biao says oppressed nations facing imperialist armed aggression must rise and fight a people's war rather than submit as slaves.

class-collaboration.rationale: Sunrise holds that class neutrality does not exist and the Essentials text says the direction of the world depends on class struggle, so the ideology puts class struggle first.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Essentials text reaffirms historical materialism: the struggle between groups over their relationship to the means of production is the chief factor shaping history.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Sunrise says a new bourgeoisie arises under the dictatorship of the proletariat and cultural revolutions are needed, and the Essentials text calls for continued class struggle under socialism.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Breakthrough 4 of Sunrise requires massive reparations from the first world as a whole to the exploited and oppressed nations.

colonial-socialism-democratic-stage.rationale: The Essentials text says the world's masses first fight for global new democracy rather than socialism, and Lin Biao says the national-democratic revolution must be completed before the socialist one.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Nick Brown says the goal is not for everyone to live like consumeristic Amerikans and that First World affluence is tied to exploitation and possible ecological collapse.

democracy-best.rationale: Sunrise calls for a joint dictatorship of exploited nations over the exploiter populations and rejects contending for power within a traditional democratic framework.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: In the Stolen at Gunpoint interview Sakai objects that Israeli law gives land to Zionists from Russia or Brooklyn with no provable connection to Palestine while denying it to Palestinians living there.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: MIM(Prisons) treats revolutions that install a dictatorship of the proletariat as the aim, in the First World too, and counts the first successful revolution as one leading to such a dictatorship.

dominated-front.rationale: Sunrise upholds a broad united front against imperialism, with the third-world countryside encircling the first-world cities, and Lin Biao treats Asia, Africa and Latin America as the world's countryside whose struggles decide world revolution.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Sunrise calls for return of the land, and Sakai says in the Stolen at Gunpoint interview that only the indigenous and Mexican peoples may decide the Southwest's future because it is theirs.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Sunrise calls for return of the land and Sakai says in the interview appendix (Stolen at Gunpoint) that only the indigenous, Mexican and Chicano peoples have the right to decide the destiny of the Southwest.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Sunrise requires a joint dictatorship of exploited nations over exploiter populations and return of the land, and Sakai says in the Stolen at Gunpoint interview that white people have no vote in the destiny of the colonized Southwest.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: RAIM lists work against Zionism among its activities, and Sakai (Stolen at Gunpoint interview) counts Israel among settler countries whose unjust laws give land to Zionists and deny it to Palestinians.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: MIM's third cardinal principle, as MIM(Prisons) quotes it, says imperialism extracts super-profits from the Third World and uses part of them to buy off whole populations of oppressor-nation 'so-called workers', who form a labor aristocracy.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The Essentials text says all economic wealth is the product of labor and measures workers' wages against the abstract value of labor.

majority-settlement.rationale: In the Stolen at Gunpoint interview Sakai calls settler invasion of other nations' lands illegitimate and says the oppressor cannot decide for the oppressed.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The Essentials text calls historical materialism its base and names the struggle over the means of producing and distributing wealth as the chief factor shaping history, though it speaks of struggle rather than of structural change as such.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The Essentials text says the basic choice facing humanity is between socialism and communism or widespread ruin, and ends by upholding Marxism-Leninism-Maoism-Third Worldism.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Lin Biao justifies tit-for-tat armed struggle by oppressed peoples against imperialist armed aggression.

no-transition-to-communism.rationale: Sunrise reaffirms the dictatorship of the proletariat and the Essentials text calls socialism a transitional period between the overthrow of capitalism and the restructuring of society.

one-party-rule.rationale: Lin Biao says the new-democratic revolution must be led by the proletariat and its Marxist-Leninist party and by no other class or party, and that it ends in the dictatorship of the proletariat.

opposition-only-legal-channels.rationale: Sunrise says people's war must be carried through to the end and Lin Biao calls it the touchstone of genuine revolutionaries to fight armed suppression in kind.

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: Breakthrough 7 of Sunrise says the proletariat cannot contend for state power within a traditional democratic framework.

party-own-road.rationale: MIM(Prisons) holds that each national struggle needs independence, that each liberation movement's leaders interpret their own conditions, and opposes a communist international subsuming one party under another.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: Its adherents' own line is People's War: contributors in MIM(Prisons)'s pages call for hastening People's War, and MIM(Prisons) defends People's War in Peru.

production-for-use.rationale: The Essentials text defines socialism as democratic and rational control over the production and allocation of use values, and puts the common good ahead of the profit-seeking of the few.

profit-exploitation.rationale: A Third Worldist reply quoted by MIM(Prisons) locates super-profits in the super-exploitation of the Third World proletariat and in a higher rate of surplus-value, the Marxist account of profit as exploitation.

property-sabotage-justified.rationale: A blog post in the Maoism-Third Worldism blog lists theft and destruction of property of the middle class and sabotage of First World countries among its pillars of practice.

public-ownership.rationale: The Essentials text says the proletariat must organize to seize the instruments of production and build its own state forms, with socialism meaning democratic and rational control over production.

race-social-construct.rationale: In Settlers ch. VI Sakai says nationality differences were disguised as racial ones and calls the 'white race' categorizing pseudo-scientific and racist.

remove-indigenous-peoples.rationale: Sunrise demands return of the land and support for national liberation of oppressed nations, and Sakai in the Stolen at Gunpoint interview calls the conquest of Native and Mexican lands illegitimate.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: In the interview appendix (Stolen at Gunpoint) Sakai says there is plenty of land in Amerika for everyone who lives there and that the problem is the Empire, not each other.

resist-oppression-despite-death.rationale: Lin Biao asks whether the oppressed should submit as slaves or fight, and calls daring to wage a people's war the test of genuine revolutionaries.

revolution-legitimate.rationale: MIM(Prisons) argues for overthrowing imperialism by revolution and treats the success of revolutions as the test of its line.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: MIM(Prisons) says settler-colonialism defines occupied Turtle Island (the United States) and must be recognized as one form of imperialism.

simple-living.rationale: Nick Brown says the aim is to provide basic material and social needs and treats a new phone every year or closets of clothes as consumerist excess, while backing a lower First World standard of living.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Breakthrough 7 of Sunrise says the proletariat cannot win state power inside a traditional democratic framework and the old world must be destroyed with dual institutional and cultural power.

socialism-needs-revolutionary-war.rationale: Sunrise says without people's war the proletariat cannot achieve state power, and Lin Biao calls seizure of power by armed force the central task and highest form of revolution for all countries.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: MIM(Prisons) frames socialism as arriving through a dictatorship of the proletariat, the working class holding state power.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Breakthrough 5 of Sunrise says capitalist counter-revolution happened in the Soviet Union in the 1950s, which it does not call by the label 'state-capitalist'.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Breakthrough 7 of Sunrise says every aspect of society including the state is stamped by power and is either principally proletarian or principally non-proletarian.

vanguard-party.rationale: MIM(Prisons) stresses the independence and leadership role of the proletarian party in national liberation and works as a cell of revolutionaries; its pages speak of an all-sided revolutionary organization leading the people.

worker-farmer-alliance.rationale: Lin Biao names the worker-peasant alliance as a basic characteristic of the Chinese and October revolutions and the peasants as the main force in colonial countries.

workers-anti-imperialist-capitalist-alli.rationale: Lin Biao says the new-democratic revolution must rally all anti-imperialist patriotic forces including the national bourgeoisie, whom the proletariat welcomes.

workers-nation.rationale: Nick Brown says any genuine revolution rests on the poorest 80 percent of humanity and that first-world workers share more outlook with their own bourgeoisie than with the global proletariat.

workers-own-party.rationale: Lin Biao says revolutions must be led by the working class with a Marxist-Leninist party as its nucleus and by no other party.

workers-parties-campaign-reforms.rationale: RAIM never takes part in reformist issues such as unions or electoral campaigns, and the Essentials text says substantive change cannot come from political reforms and opposes all economism.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: MIM(Prisons) states that imperialism places some nations in a position of receiving surplus value and others of losing it, and that imperialism extracts super-profits from the Third World.

passes.gapException: 2026-11-24 pass rested on critics' scope and found none of the ideology's own texts (Brandon, 2026-11-27)

scope: Maoism–Third Worldism (MTW) as the tendency that Monkey Smashes Heaven declared on 1 January 2008 in 'Sunrise in the East' (s6), naming 'Maoism-Third Worldism' a new, fourth stage of revolutionary science after Marxism-Leninism-Maoism, with eight 'breakthroughs' (global class analysis in which First World 'workers' are not allies of the Third World masses, global people's war on Lin Biao's model, the principal contradiction between imperialism and the oppressed nations, among them). It was carried by the Leading Light Communist Organization (LLCO) until that group moved on to 'Leading Light Communism' (s10, s4) and by the Revolutionary Anti-Imperialist Movement (RAIM), whose interview calls it 'a synthesis of the lessons of 20th century revolution' (s7); a present-day blog still proselytizes for it (s9). Its texts are J. Sakai's Settlers (s11), which RAIM and the sources tie to it, and Lin Biao's 'Long Live the Victory of People's War!' (s12). The profile does not cover the original MIM's own line, the MIM Thought of MIM(Prisons), which agrees with the eight breakthroughs yet rejects the label and the claim of a new stage (s8, s4, s5), nor LLCO's later Leading Light Communism, nor critics' accounts of the tendency (for example Struggle Sessions and Moufawad-Paul), which only help find what it holds.
